BIO 101: Introductory Biology
Instructor: Prof. Diana M. Harrison
Semester: Fall 2026
Class Meeting: MWF 10:00-11:00 AM, Science Building Room 215

COURSE OVERVIEW
This course introduces fundamental principles of biology, including cellular structure, genetics, evolution, and ecology. Students will develop laboratory skills and critical thinking through hands-on experiments and discussions.

COURSE OBJECTIVES
Upon completion, students will be able to:
- Explain basic cellular mechanisms and molecular biology
- Apply evolutionary principles to real-world scenarios
- Design and conduct biological experiments
- Interpret scientific data and literature

COURSE MATERIALS
Required Textbook: Campbell Biology: A Global Approach (12th ed.)
Lab Manual: Included with course materials
Software: None

GRADING BREAKDOWN
Participation and Discussion    10%
Laboratory Reports              25%
Midterm Exam                     20%
Quizzes (3 x 5%)               15%
Research Paper                  15%
Final Exam                       15%

COURSE SCHEDULE & DEADLINES

Unit 1: Cell Biology (Sept 14 - Oct 5)
- Sept 14: First class, syllabus review
- Sept 21: Lab 1: Cell Structure due
- 9/28: Quiz 1 (Chapters 3-4)
- 10/3: Lab 2: Osmosis and Diffusion due

Unit 2: Genetics (10/6 - 11/2)
- October 13: Lab 3: Drosophila Genetics due
- 10/20: Quiz 2 (Chapters 8-9)
- 10/27: Midterm Exam (covers Units 1-2)
- November 2: Lab 4: Protein Synthesis due

Unit 3: Evolution and Ecology (11/3 - 12/1)
- Nov 10: Research Paper Outline due
- 11/17: Lab 5: Population Dynamics due
- 11/24: THANKSGIVING - No class
- 11/30: Quiz 3 (Chapters 21-23)
- 12/1: Research Paper Final due

EXAMINATION DATES
Midterm Exam: October 27, 2026 (in class)
Final Exam: December 15, 2026, 9:00-11:00 AM

LABORATORY REQUIREMENTS
All students must attend weekly labs (Wed 1:00-3:00 PM). Lab reports are due one week after the lab session. Missing more than two labs without documented excuse will result in an automatic F for the course.

ATTENDANCE POLICY
Attendance is required for all classes and labs. More than three unexcused absences will lower your final grade by 5 points per absence.

ACADEMIC INTEGRITY
The Academic Honor Code applies to all work in this course. Plagiarism and cheating will result in a failing grade for the assignment and possible disciplinary action.

ACCOMMODATIONS
Students with documented disabilities should contact the Office of Disability Services to arrange appropriate accommodations.
